result.builder:
Criteria the build must meet (from the issue, word for word):
- math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi
- clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi
- README.md documents every function math.js exports
- npm test passes

Steps:
1. Read math.js, README.md, package.json and test/math.test.js. math.js is CommonJS and currently exports add, subtract and multiply via module.exports. Tests use node:test (`npm test` runs `node --test`).
2. In math.js add a function clamp(x, lo, hi) with a short doc comment, in the same style as the others. If lo > hi, throw a RangeError (e.g. `throw new RangeError('clamp: lo must not be greater than hi')`). Otherwise return lo when x < lo, hi when x > hi, and x itself when it is in range (lo and hi inclusive). Add clamp to module.exports alongside the existing functions; do not remove or rename any existing export.
3. In test/math.test.js import clamp and add tests: a value below the range returns lo (e.g. clamp(-5, 0, 100) === 0), a value above returns hi (clamp(140, 0, 100) === 100), a value inside returns itself (clamp(42, 0, 100) === 42), boundary values return themselves, lo === hi returns that value, and clamp(5, 10, 0) throws a RangeError (assert.throws(..., RangeError)).
4. In README.md, under the existing `## API` section, document every function math.js exports. Note that subtract is exported but currently missing from the README: add a `### subtract(a, b)` section (returns `a` minus `b`, with a short example) and a `### clamp(x, lo, hi)` section (returns `x` limited to the range `lo` to `hi`, inclusive; throws a RangeError when `lo` is greater than `hi`; with an example such as `clamp(140, 0, 100); // 100`). Keep add and multiply sections. Use the same `### name(params)` heading style.
5. Run `npm test` and make sure it exits 0 with all tests passing. Also check by hand that `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./math.js')))"` lists names that each have a README `###` heading.
6. Open one pull request containing these changes.
result.verifier:
Work at the PR head, from the repository root. Run `npm install` only if package.json gained dependencies (currently it has none).

Check 1 — expect: "math.js exports clamp(x, lo, hi), which returns x limited to the range lo to hi"
Run:
node -e "const m=require('./math.js');const c=m.clamp;if(typeof c!=='function'){console.log('NOFN');process.exit(1)}const cases=[[-5,0,100,0],[140,0,100,100],[42,0,100,42],[0,0,100,0],[100,0,100,100],[7,7,7,7],[-3,-10,-1,-3],[-20,-10,-1,-10],[0.5,0,1,0.5],[2.5,0,1,1]];let bad=0;for(const [x,lo,hi,e] of cases){const r=c(x,lo,hi);if(r!==e){bad++;console.log('BAD',x,lo,hi,'got',r,'want',e)}}console.log(bad?'FAIL':'OK');process.exit(bad?1:0)"
PASS: prints OK and exits 0 (clamp is an exported function and every case returns x limited to [lo, hi]). FAIL: clamp is missing or not a function, any case prints BAD, or the command errors.

Check 2 — expect: "clamp(x, lo, hi) throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi"
Run:
node -e "const {clamp}=require('./math.js');let bad=0;for(const a of [[5,10,0],[0,1,0],[50,100,-100],[1,0.2,0.1]]){try{clamp(...a);console.log('NOTHROW',a);bad++}catch(e){if(!(e instanceof RangeError)){console.log('WRONG',a,e&&e.constructor&&e.constructor.name);bad++}}}console.log(bad?'FAIL':'OK');process.exit(bad?1:0)"
PASS: prints OK and exits 0 (every call with lo > hi throws an instance of RangeError). FAIL: any call returns without throwing, throws something other than a RangeError, or the command errors.

Check 3 — expect: "README.md documents every function math.js exports"
Run:
node -e "const fs=require('fs');const m=require('./math.js');const r=fs.readFileSync('README.md','utf8');const fns=Object.keys(m).filter(k=>typeof m[k]==='function');const miss=fns.filter(n=>!new RegExp('^#+\\s*`?'+n+'\\s*\\(','m').test(r));console.log('exports:',fns.join(','));console.log(miss.length?'MISSING '+miss.join(','):'OK');process.exit(miss.length?1:0)"
Then open README.md and confirm each exported function (expected at least add, subtract, multiply, clamp) has a section that describes what it does.
PASS: the script prints OK and every exported function has a README entry describing it. FAIL: the script prints MISSING for any function (e.g. subtract, which was undocumented before), or an entry is only a bare heading with no description.

Check 4 — expect: "npm test passes"
Run: `npm test; echo EXIT=$?`
PASS: EXIT=0 and the node:test summary shows fail 0. FAIL: non-zero exit or any failing test.

Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions):
- Check that the PR added tests for clamp (in-range, below, above, boundaries, RangeError) in test/math.test.js.
- Note whether existing exports add, subtract, multiply still behave as before.
- Note behaviour for NaN inputs, if any, as an observation only.
